page: Amazon Web Services r8g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family, utilizing the arm64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs with a single thread per core, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The CPU is based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 model, equipped with 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and operates on the Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

In benchmark testing, the r8g.4xlarge demonstrates strong memory subsystem performance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier (top 10%), supported by uncached large-block memory read speeds of 317.2 GB/sec and write speeds of 130.27 GB/sec, both categorized as strong. Database operations in Passmark also show strong performance at 23912.07. CPU-bound benchmarks, such as stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, fall into the average range. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression is strong at 14.35 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression and Redis SET operations perform at average levels. Large language model inference speeds are average to weak, with 7B model text generation reaching 12.93 tokens per second and 70B model text generation dropping to a poor 2.37 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8g.4xlarge offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or high-performance GPU acceleration. The absence of hyperthreading ensures dedicated execution resources per vCPU, which benefits predictable performance. This instance is well suited for memory-intensive applications, including medium-sized databases, caching layers such as Redis, memory-bound data processing, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring high memory bandwidth.
